findings.desc: CHK-001:edge:0 evidence cites the 'sanity-bound' case at packages/main/src/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts:442-448 as proof that the retained sanity bound 'is exercised rather than silently absent,' but that case only asserts TRANSCRIPT.length > 200_000 and that the digest matches /^story_advance\/[0-9a-f]{12}$/ -- a well-formed-digest check that passes identically whether or not the .slice(0, MAX_REASON_CHARS) bound exists in convergence-breaker.ts:483-485. Verified empirically: removed the .slice(0, MAX_REASON_CHARS) call from convergence-breaker.ts, rebuilt, and ran this exact assertion pair in isolation against the bound-removed build -- it still PASSED. The bound-removed build IS caught, but by a different case: 'must-still-collapse beyond-sanity-bound' (smoke.ts:337-341, MUST_COLLAPSE lane), which is the evidence cited for the separate intent CHK-001:edge:1, not for edge:0. So CHK-001:edge:0 has no valid evidence of its own claimed property; that property is established elsewhere under a different intentRef. This is an evidence note that restates the intent rather than an assertion that proves it. Net risk is low (the bound is genuinely tested by edge:1), but the edge:0 evidence record itself does not cover what it claims.

packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:510 — the narrowed digit-rule regex `(?<![\w-])\d+(?![\w-])` only treats a digit run as identifier-attached when preceded/followed by a word char or ASCII hyphen; a `.` does not protect. Verified empirically: normalize("requires lattice-cli v0.3.229 or newer") and normalize("requires lattice-cli v0.3.230 or newer") both reduce to "requires lattice-cli v0.#.# or newer" (identical digest). Any rejection reason embedding a dotted version/semver string (a realistic shape given version-bump.ts already formats messages like "expected X.Y.Z") collapses two substantively different failures into one gate-failure key -- exactly the C4 over-collapse class this story exists to fix, for a token shape CHK-003/CHK-004 never exercises. gateFailureDigest is exported general-purpose, not scoped to the one current call site.

packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:510 — the digit-rule lookbehind/lookahead `(?<![\w-])...(?![\w-])` excludes a preceding/following ASCII hyphen unconditionally, which also matches a minus sign, so a negative number is treated as identifier-attached and survives instead of collapsing. Verified: normalize("retry budget -5 remaining") vs normalize("retry budget -19 remaining") do NOT collapse (stay distinct), unlike the documented free-standing-counter behavior in the surrounding comment (attempt 41, 3>=2, 0/4 lanes all correctly collapse). This under-collapses an incidental numeric difference, i.e. it is a live instance of the exact risk plan.md #4 calls out as the change's central danger ("the change makes the breaker fire less often ... a stuck agent [could] regain an unbounded retry loop"), for a token shape (negative numbers) the CHK-004 must-still-collapse lane never tests.

packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:463-468 — the function's top JSDoc still states the error message is "normalized to strip volatile tokens (hashes, ids, timestamps, bare numbers, paths)" unqualified. This is now inaccurate: CHK-002 narrowed path-stripping to token-start absolute paths only (relative repo paths and mid-token slashes like DEV/REVIEW are deliberately left untouched), and CHK-003 narrowed number-stripping to standalone numbers only (identifier-attached digits like CHK-001 are deliberately preserved). A maintainer reading only this doc comment would believe ALL paths and ALL bare numbers are still stripped, which is precisely the kind of doc/implementation mismatch this story's own root cause (an over-broad implementation vs. a narrower intended contract) illustrates. The doc comment should name the narrower rule (token-start absolute paths; standalone digit runs) so a future edit does not re-widen the regex believing it is restoring documented behavior.

packages/main/src/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts:316-318 — the new must-still-collapse case 'timestamp-and-attempt-counter' uses the exact same two literal fixture strings ("gate BLOCKED for B-bbaf at 2026-07-14T00:00:00Z (attempt 3)" / "...T09:59:59Z (attempt 41)") already asserted for digest-equality and counter-accumulation-to-2 at lines 165-166 and 172-173 in the pre-existing section 7 (unchanged by this diff). The new section 7b matrix explicitly frames itself (comment at line ~182) as replacing the removed ALPHA/BETA fixture and adding fresh must-differ/must-still-collapse coverage, but this one case adds no new coverage over the pre-existing K1 timestamp/attempt-counter assertion it duplicates -- same input strings, same digest-equality check, same counter-reaches-2 check, run twice under two different code paths for no additional signal.

packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:502 — the path-rule regex `(?:^|(?<=[\s"'(\[]))\/[^\s"')\]]*` only recognizes POSIX-style absolute paths (leading `/`). A Windows-style absolute path such as `C:\Users\jek\file1.ts` vs `C:\Users\other\file2.ts` is left completely untouched by every normalization rule (no leading slash, and digits inside `file1`/`file2` are word-attached so the digit-rule also leaves them alone) and so the two machine-specific paths do NOT collapse to one digest -- verified empirically. The design comment at :500-501 explicitly claims the rule "behaves identically on macOS and Linux" (i.e. Windows was consciously out of scope), so this may be an accepted gap rather than an oversight, but it reproduces the same host-varying-path-does-not-collapse failure mode this story exists to fix if this CLI is ever run from a Windows host.

packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts:510 the narrowed standalone-number rule `(?<![\w-])\d+(?![\w-])` does not normalize a digit run directly attached to a UNIT-LETTER suffix (e.g. 45s, 5m, 2h) because the follow-char is a word character, so the negative lookahead blocks the match. Three real, story_advance-reachable rejection messages embed exactly this shape via formatLeaseAge/formatLockAge (heartbeat `${age} ago`, age like 45s/5m/2h): (1) packages/main/src/core/story-owner-lease.ts:591-598,616-640 formatLeaseAge/formatNonOwnerError (thrown from cli/ownership-gate.ts non-owner story_advance rejection -- the common no-lease-owned-by-me path), (2) packages/main/src/cli/ownership-gate.ts:301-306 active-lease --takeover rejection, (3) packages/main/src/core/main-write-lock.ts:71-113 formatLockAge/buildMainWriteLockContentionMessage (DONE-phase main-write-lock contention), (4) packages/main/src/core/validation-execution-lock.ts:233-262 formatLockAge/buildValidationLockContentionMessage (TEST-phase validation-lock contention). Verified against the built packages/main/dist/core/convergence-breaker.js: gateFailureDigest(story_advance, msg-with-45s) !== gateFailureDigest(story_advance, msg-with-46s) for all four message shapes (confirmed by direct node execution), so a story_advance retried against an actively-heartbeating foreign lease or a held lock gets a NEW digest key on essentially every retry and maxGateFailureCount never reaches 2 -- assessBreaker never trips gate-repeat for exactly the runaway-retry-loop scenario the breaker exists to catch. Confirmed this is a functional REGRESSION: the OLD unconditional /\d+/g rule DID collapse these same two messages to one key (verified directly), so narrowing broke a previously-working case. This also falsifies the CHK-003 verificationIntent edge claim recorded in plan.md #3 (Confirmed no production rejection message embeds a volatile counter attached to an identifier: the only attached-counter shapes in the tree are step record ids at planned-steps-executor.ts:1298 and :1309, and that module throws no Error) -- that module indeed throws nothing, but the heartbeat-age shape above DOES throw reachable Errors and was missed by that survey. None of CHK-004s must-still-collapse matrix cases (packages/main/src/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts) exercise a digit-attached-to-unit-letter shape -- its only counter/timestamp case uses ISO-8601 timestamps plus a free-standing (attempt N) counter -- so the regression guard does not catch this. Fix: normalize the digit+unit-letter age shape (e.g. \\b\\d+[smh]\\b) before/alongside the standalone-number rule, or normalize via the formatted age helper output generally.

packages/main/src/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.ts userSees text for CHK-002 and CHK-003 (and to a lesser extent CHK-001) describes prose that a human reading the console output would supposedly see (e.g. CHK-002 userSees: the smoke prints passing checks stating that DEV/REVIEW and DEV/TEST digest differently...and that the same lock path under /Users and under /private/var still digests identically; CHK-003 userSees: a passing check stating that a rejection naming CHK-001 and one naming CHK-002 digest differently). I ran node packages/main/dist/tasks/convergence-breaker-smoke.js and the actual printed lines for these cases are terse machine-readable tags with no literal mention of the compared values, e.g. `  must-differ         phase-pair [guard: path-rule] keys=2 counter=1 breaker=proceed` and `  must-differ         checklist-ordinal [guard: digit-rule] keys=2 counter=1 breaker=proceed` and `  must-still-collapse machine-absolute-path [guard: collapse-lane] keys=1 counter=2 breaker=trips`. The literal strings DEV/REVIEW, DEV/TEST, /Users, /private/var, CHK-001, CHK-002 never appear anywhere in the printed output -- only abstract case-name tags (phase-pair, machine-absolute-path, checklist-ordinal) do, and a reader would have to open the source file to learn which literal values each tag represents. The functional claim (keys differ / collapse, counter value) IS correctly proven, but the userSees text overstates what the printed output literally states, describing prose sentences that do not appear on screen. CHK-004s userSees ("lists the must-differ and must-still-collapse digest cases by name, each reporting the resulting gate-failure counter value") is accurate and matches the real output. Suggest tightening CHK-001/002/003 userSees to describe the actual tag+keys/counter/breaker format rather than implying literal value names are printed.

cross-host (codex-cli host-B) finding, recorded by the main agent because codex-cli is not a registered dispatch actor: packages/main/src/core/convergence-breaker.ts — MAX_REASON_CHARS slices the RAW reason as UTF-16 code units before normalization, so a reason of the form 'x'.repeat(16383) + an astral character leaves a lone high surrogate (0xd83d) as the final unit, which hashes as replacement encoding rather than the original character. Deterministic, so no cross-call instability, but the bound is not Unicode code-point safe. Fix: drop a trailing lone high surrogate after the slice.
